name: 5-channel TCRT5000 IR line tracker
description: Five Vishay TCRT5000 reflective IR sensors 15 mm apart on one 95 x 20 mm board, for line-following robots. Each phototransistor collector (pulled up to VCC) feeds one gate of a 74HC14D hex Schmitt-trigger inverter, whose push-pull output is OUTn: LOW over a black line (or with nothing in range, about 1-1.5 cm max), HIGH over a white surface, with a per-channel LED lit over white. No trimmers. Runs on 3.3-5 V; outputs swing to VCC. Sold as: 5-channel TCRT5000 IR line tracking sensor board (common blue 95 x 20 mm clone, 7-pin header GND, 5V, OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, OUT4, OUT5, single 74HC14D, no potentiometers).
eli5: Five little eyes in a row look down at the floor and tell your robot which of them is over the black line, so it knows whether to steer left or right.

supplierQuery: 5 channel TCRT5000 line tracking sensor module 74HC14
buildNotes: Header order as printed: GND, 5V, OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, OUT4, OUT5. All seven pins are in one straight row (usually a right-angle header).
Despite the '5V' label the board runs from 3.3-5 V. On an ESP32 or Pico power it from 3V3: the 74HC14 outputs are push-pull and swing to the supply, so 5 V would put 5 V on the GPIOs.
OUTn is LOW over a black line and HIGH over white (its LED lights over white). Lifted off the floor, all five read LOW like black.
There are no trimmers: mount the sensors about 5-15 mm above a matte floor with a dark line at least 15-20 mm wide.
The five IR LEDs are always on: the board draws up to about 100 mA, so feed it from a rail that can supply that.
Sunlight and incandescent light contain IR and can upset the readings; glossy black tape may read as white.

driver.code:
# 5-channel TCRT5000 IR line tracking sensor board (blue 95 x 20 mm board, header GND, 5V, OUT1-OUT5,
# one 74HC14D hex Schmitt-trigger inverter, no trimmers), MicroPython driver.
# Board circuit: each TCRT5000's IR LED is lit all the time. Its phototransistor collector is pulled
# up to VCC; that node drives one 74HC14 Schmitt inverter input, and the inverter output is OUTn
# (push-pull, swings 0 V to VCC).
#   Black line (IR absorbed): transistor off, input high -> OUTn = LOW, channel LED off.
#   White / light surface (IR reflected): transistor conducts, input low -> OUTn = HIGH, LED on.
#   Nothing within range (lifted off the floor): reads like black, OUTn = LOW.
# Power the board from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V microcontroller: the outputs swing to VCC.
from machine import Pin


class LineTracker5:
    def __init__(self, out1, out2, out3, out4, out5):
        # Push-pull 74HC14 outputs: no pull-up needed.
        self.pins = [p if not isinstance(p, int) else Pin(p, Pin.IN)
                     for p in (out1, out2, out3, out4, out5)]

    def raw(self):
        """Logic levels of OUT1..OUT5: 1 = white/reflective, 0 = black line or nothing in range."""
        return [p.value() for p in self.pins]

    def black(self):
        """List of 5 booleans, True where that sensor sits over the black line (OUT low)."""
        return [p.value() == 0 for p in self.pins]

    def pattern(self):
        """String such as '00100': '1' = black line under OUT1..OUT5 (left to right as printed)."""
        return ''.join('1' if b else '0' for b in self.black())

    def position(self):
        """Line position from -2 (under OUT1) to +2 (under OUT5), averaged over the sensors
        that see black; None when no sensor sees the line, or when all five do
        (lifted off the floor, or crossing a wide marker)."""
        b = self.black()
        n = sum(b)
        if n == 0 or n == 5:
            return None
        return sum(i - 2 for i in range(5) if b[i]) / n

example.code:
from line_tracker5 import LineTracker5
import time

tracker = LineTracker5({OUT1}, {OUT2}, {OUT3}, {OUT4}, {OUT5})
while True:
    print('Line: %s' % tracker.pattern())
    time.sleep(0.5)
